title: Big Al McMordie Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: Big Al McMordie review, checked 7 Nov 2026: BigAl.com prices from $30 picks to $2,395 a year, refund terms, what his record claims show, and buyer reports.
dek: Al McMordie has sold picks at BigAl.com since 1992 and now sells picks from about 20 handicappers, from $30 a pick to $2,395 for a year. The site grades its own handicappers and publishes daily results, and one outside monitor shows him profitable this year. There is no performance guarantee.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Al McMordie or any BigAl.com handicapper. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Big Al's Sports Picks is a real, long running business. It names Al McMordie as the owner, lists a Los Angeles mailing address and a phone number he says he answers himself, publishes its prices and posts yesterday's results for every handicapper it sells.

Whether his picks make money over time is harder to answer. Most numbers on BigAl.com are graded by BigAl.com, and the career totals and awards on his page are seller claims with no full pick log behind them that we could open. One outside site, SportsWatchMonitor, showed him with a positive return for 2026 and for 2023, 2024 and 2025, but those returns were small, between 2.6% and 4.2% a year, and we could not open the pick logs behind them.

Treat Big Al as an established seller with some outside tracking, not a proven long term winner. If you buy, buy short, record every pick yourself with the line and time you received it, and judge it after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: BigAl.com does not sell a guarantee. The refund policy says "There are no performance guarantees" and that refunds "will not be provided due to poor predictive performance." Single picks are refunded only if the game is suspended, cancelled, postponed more than four days, already started at purchase, or if a baseball pitcher changes after the pick is posted. Those exceptions do not apply to subscriptions.

The FAQ offers something softer. If a week or 30 day subscription fails to show a profit, graded at $1,000 a game, BigAl.com says it would "be happy to offer you a discount" on a new weekly or 30 day subscription. That is a discount on buying more, not money back, and it never covers what you lost on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The awards list is long, but almost every line is a rank in one sport over one window, such as "#2 NBA Basketball Win Percentage" or "#1 NBA Playoffs Return on Risk." With many sports, many windows and several ranking categories, some first place finishes are likely for any active handicapper. The awards page names the monitors behind them, including The Sports Monitor, Sports Watch and Sports Watch Monitor,, but we did not check those historical rankings, and this review does not rely on them.

The "angle" and "system" records in pick titles, such as 9-0 or 15-1 ATS, describe how a past trend did, not how Al's picks did. Trends found by searching old games tend to look perfect in hindsight and weaken going forward.

Small inconsistencies: the homepage says 21 handicappers and the FAQ says 20, and the FAQ names handicappers, such as Larry Ness and Oskeim Sports, who are not on the current roster. The FAQ appears partly out of date.
record: What a buyer can check outside BigAl.com: SportsWatchMonitor, a monitoring site, listed Al McMordie on its homepage on 7 Nov 2026 with a 2026 return of 4.0% and $21,582 profit, and yearly returns of 3.1% (2025), 4.2% (2024) and 2.6% (2023). SportsCapping, a pick marketplace, ranked "Big Al McMordie" 13th on its season profit board the same day at 676-579, 53.9% wins, average odds of -113, 1.8% ROI and $2,676 profit on flat $100 bets. Both sites also sell picks, the SportsWatchMonitor page does not state the bet size behind its dollars, and we could not open the full pick logs behind either figure, so we treat them as third party numbers, not audits.

What is the seller's own marketing: BigAl.com grades its handicappers itself, at $1,000 a game, using the best line among BetMGM, Caesars and DraftKings at the time of the pick, according to its FAQ. It posts the previous day's results each morning (Al went 4-3-1, +$650 on 6 Nov 2026) and leaderboards by time window. We did not find a full, searchable archive of every past pick with its line and post time. The career totals, such as 5332-4404, and the awards list are not backed by a log we could open.

Contest results, such as the 2004 Stardust Invitational, would be independently verifiable if the organizers published them, but we did not find those records today. We found no court or regulator action involving Al McMordie or BigAl.com in our searches.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition neither Al McMordie nor any BigAl.com handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Al's page markets basketball seasons won in the mid 50s by win rate. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Big Al is thin and mostly old. The testimonials on BigAl.com are chosen by the seller, and the forum discussion we could open dates from 2005 and 2012. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: The homepage shows about ten testimonials, including podcast host Joe House and several clients who say they have used Al since the 1990s and praise his data driven approach and futures bets. One says Al had a losing NFL year before winning ones. These are selected and published by the seller.

On TheRX forum, a member objected to an ad that called a Golden State pick a cashed "Game of the Month" when, he said, the line sat at 2.5 or 3 for most of the day, and others mocked calling the next play a "BLOWOUT" winner. Another member wrote that his notes had the line at 3 for part of the day. This is a 21 year old dispute about one game.

In the same thread a member wrote that Al is "one of the best at selling plays" and gets carried away with hype, but that he does not run a boiler room, does not sell opposing plays, and answers his own phone. No results were posted.
Trustpilot showed no page for bigal.com, we found no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to BigAl.com, and we found no Reddit thread discussing the service.

In the 2005 TheRX thread a member called Al a "BAD handicapper" and a scam, claiming buyers got little more than trends and systems from a computer program. He pointed to recent losses that, he said, the next promo did not mention.

Later in the same thread a member said he had bought plays from Big Al a few times and once talked with him on the phone at length. He said there was no staff of sales callers and no push toward a high roller package, though he disliked the promotion style and advised buyer beware.

conflicts: BigAl.com sells picks from its whole roster and ranks the same handicappers in its own articles and leaderboards. A ranking published by the store that sells the picks is marketing, not an independent board.

The homepage promotes "Top Offshore Sportsbooks," and the sportsbooks page ranks offshore books with tracked links, including one at aff.betanysports.eu/big-al and one carrying the referral code ALMCMORDIE, plus a BetUS bonus that asks you to use the code "BigAl." Affiliate deals like these usually pay the site when readers sign up or lose. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators, so check the law where you live.
SportsWatchMonitor and SportsCapping, the outside sites that track him, also sell handicapper picks, so they are not neutral auditors either.
strengths: A named owner, a mailing address, a phone number with stated hours and a full price list.
Yesterday's results for every handicapper, losses included, are posted each morning, and the grading method (line at release, $1,000 a game) is written down in the FAQ.
An outside monitor showed small positive returns for 2023 through 2026, which is more than most pick sellers can point to.
Free daily picks with written analysis let a reader see the style before paying.
concerns: No full public archive of every pick with line and post time. Career totals and awards are seller claims.
No performance guarantee and no refunds for losing picks. The FAQ offers only a discount on another subscription.
The site carries offshore sportsbook affiliate links and promo codes.
Pick titles lean on hyped past trends such as "100% Perfect" angles, which say little about future results.
Even the outside numbers show thin margins, a few percent a year, which worse lines or late buying could erase for a customer.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes in the sense that BigAl.com is a real, long running business with a named owner, an address, published prices and daily posted results. We could not verify his long term career record, because the site does not publish a full log of every pick.
How much does Big Al McMordie cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 his single picks were $30 each, and BigAl.com subscriptions ran from $100 for 7 days of baseball or hockey and $395 for 30 days of all sports up to $1,500 to $1,995 for a season and $2,395 for a year of all sports.
Does Big Al McMordie have a verified record?

Not a full one. BigAl.com grades its own picks and posts daily results, and two outside sites, SportsWatchMonitor and SportsCapping, showed him profitable in 2026 by small margins, but we could not open the pick logs behind any of these numbers, and Watchdog has no graded record for him.
Is Big Al McMordie worth it?

For the money you get daily picks with written analysis from a long time handicapper, with a $30 single pick as the cheapest entry. What is unproven is whether a buyer, getting the line available at purchase, beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of picks, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
